Why are there two different capacity values?

• Chemical Remaining (RM): This is the exact amount of charge (in mAh) currently stored in the battery at this very moment. It changes dynamically as you use or charge the phone.

• Remaining Capacity (FCC, shown in the top card): This is the Full Charge Capacity — the maximum total charge the battery can hold today when charged to 100% (e.g. 5530 mAh out of 5840 mAh original design). It decreases very slowly over months and years due to natural chemical aging.

Formula:
Current Level % = (RM / FCC) × 100

Represents the instantaneous electrical voltage of the battery cell(s) in millivolts (mV).

• Typical values: Ranges between ~3300 mV (nearly empty battery) and ~4450 mV (100% full charge).

• Dual-Cell Architecture (e.g. Find X / dual series SuperVOOC): Displays separate voltages for Cell 0 and Cell 1 along with cell balance differential (Δ mV). A delta close to 0 mV indicates optimal balance.

• Single-Cell Architecture (e.g. Reno 14): Displays the direct voltage of the single installed cell.

This is the cell's intrinsic maximum chemical capacity under zero-load conditions (without internal resistance or voltage drop).

• Why is it higher than rated capacity? Under normal operation, a battery loses energy due to internal resistance (IR) and load voltage drops. Qmax represents the absolute theoretical capacity extractable at near-zero current.

• What is it used for? The Oppo BMS fuel gauge uses Qmax as the primary reference anchor to periodically recalibrate battery health (SOH) and full charge capacity (FCC).

Indicates the safety undervoltage shutdown threshold configured in the Oppo BMS chip (typically ~3300 mV).

• Purpose: If a lithium-ion/polymer cell drops below 2.5V - 3.0V, it suffers irreversible chemical damage (copper collector dissolution and internal short circuits).

• Emergency shutdown: When cell voltage reaches this critical threshold, the protection circuit forces an immediate device shutdown to protect the cell, displaying 0% on screen.
Tap 🔄 at top (or here) to refresh with a new reading

Measures the physical opposition to current flow inside the battery cell (Equivalent Series Resistance).

• Physical Formula:
ESR (mΩ) = (|V_ocv - V_now| / |I_now|) × 1000

• Reference Values (at rest / discharging):
- New / healthy cell: 50 – 250 mΩ
- Degraded / aged cell: > 450 – 600 mΩ

• During Charging (Elevated values are normal):
During charging it is completely normal to see elevated values (> 600–1200 mΩ). The charger applies a forced overpotential and chemical polarization to drive current into the cell. To evaluate true ohmic resistance, refer to readings when unplugged (under steady discharge).

• Fluctuations & Reliability:
A single momentary spike on battery is normal during rapid CPU transients. True health should be assessed by observing the average and stability over time.

Monitors the voltage uniformity between individual cells in series-connected battery systems.

• Single-Cell Architecture (e.g. Reno 14):
The device uses a single high-capacity cell (1S). Cell divergence is physically impossible, ensuring 100% uniform degradation and zero imbalance risk.

• Dual-Cell Architecture (e.g. Find X / 2S SuperVOOC):
Uses two cells in series to allow ultra-fast charging (up to 10V). The BMS actively monitors the voltage difference (Δ mV) between Cell 0 and Cell 1:
- Δ < 15 mV: Optimal Balance
- Δ 15 - 40 mV: Normal Drift
- Δ > 40 mV: Imbalanced (Cell Divergence detected)
Severe imbalance reduces usable total capacity to the level of the weakest cell.

How does the BMS track battery percentage and capacity?

• The Coulomb Counter:
The battery management system (BMS) continuously integrates the electrical current flowing in and out of the battery over time (amperes × hours = mAh).

• Drift Accumulation:
Over dozens of partial charge cycles (e.g. 20% - 80%), tiny measurement errors accumulate, leading to 'BMS drift'. The fuel gauge loses its chemical zero and saturation anchor points.

• How to Recalibrate (BMS Sync Procedure):
1. Discharge the phone normally until ~5% - 10%.
2. Charge continuously to 100% without interruptions.
3. Keep the phone plugged in at 100% for an additional 30-45 minutes (saturation phase) so the BMS can lock the OCV voltage curve and reset the coulomb counter to zero drift.

Capacity (mAh) or health % can slightly increase between readings. Here is why:

• BMS Recalibration (Not Regeneration):
Lithium cells cannot physically regenerate. After a full 100% charge and rest, the BMS updates OCV points, correcting prior drift underestimations.

• Temperature & Ion Mobility:
At 25°C–30°C ions move faster than in the cold (10°C–18°C). A warm cell has lower internal resistance and delivers slightly more usable mAh.

• Discharge Load:
Light phone usage extracts more energy before reaching cutoff voltage than heavy loads.

Small fluctuations (±20–60 mAh) are completely normal: they reflect temperature and sensor recalibrations, not battery self-repair.

The red warning symbol indicates that this value is retrieved via standard Android APIs (BATTERY_PROPERTY_CHARGE_COUNTER).

• Instantaneous Reading:
This value represents the instantaneous Coulomb counter (the electric charge present in the battery at this exact moment), NOT the total Full Charge Capacity (FCC).

• Strong Fluctuations:
It changes dynamically with current charge level, temperature, and system load. Do not confuse this instantaneous reading with the battery's total capacity at 100%.

The red warning symbol indicates that standard Android APIs do not expose the manufacturer's chemical State of Health (SOH).

• Why N/A is shown:
Android does not provide a public API for factory battery health. To read the genuine hardware SOH and full capacity, the app requires direct access to the device's Battery Management System (BMS) registers via Shizuku.

• Non-Oppo/Unsupported Devices:
On devices where Shizuku BMS registers are not supported or accessible, health cannot be verified accurately.

Battery Health reflects the true chemical State of Health (SOH) of your battery.

• Measured by BMS:
Calculated directly from the hardware fuel-gauge chip by comparing the current chemical Full Charge Capacity (FCC) against the factory rated capacity (IEC 61960).

• Retention:
Modern high-grade cells retain >80% capacity even after 1,600 full charge cycles.

The red warning symbol indicates that the operating system or device manufacturer (such as Samsung) does not expose the genuine battery charge cycle count via standard Android APIs.

• Why 0 or N/A is shown:
Many manufacturers, notably Samsung, restrict access to the cycle counter in public APIs (returning a fixed 0) and store the true cycle count in protected system partitions (EFS / Knox) that standard third-party apps cannot access.

• Supported Devices:
On devices with supported Battery Management System (BMS) hardware nodes (e.g. Oppo/OnePlus via Shizuku), the app directly extracts the exact cycle counter. On Samsung devices without accessible hardware nodes, the cycle count cannot be extracted.

What is a battery charge cycle?

• Cycle Definition:
One complete charge cycle is counted every time a cumulative 100% of the battery's capacity is discharged and recharged (e.g., discharging from 100% to 50% twice equals 1 full cycle).

• Battery Degradation:
Modern lithium-ion and silicon-carbon cells are rated to retain approximately 80% of their initial design capacity after 800 to 1,600 full charge cycles.

How is the battery life estimate calculated?

• Real-time BMS Data:
The estimate is based on the total cycles and current health recorded directly by the phone's BMS chip (not on entries saved in history or trash).

• Mathematical Formula:
1. Wear rate: computes the average number of cycles completed per 1% of health lost since new.
2. Remaining cycles: multiplies this rate by the remaining health percentage before reaching 80% (standard industry battery replacement threshold).

The estimate reflects real chemical wear since the device was first powered on.

What does "True Saturation" mean and why does it differ from Android's 100%?

• The Display 100%:
Smartphone manufacturers (including Oppo) program Android to display "100%" as soon as constant current (CC) mode finishes (~4.40V). At this exact moment, the battery is chemically only 88%–92% full.

• Saturation Phase (CV Tapering):
To reach true chemical saturation, the battery enters the Constant Voltage (CV) phase, absorbing decreasing current (from 1500 mA down to <80 mA) for an extra 20–40 minutes.

• Direct Fuel Gauge Chip Reading (chip_soc):
This app queries the physical fuel gauge register. When "Saturated" is indicated, the electrochemical cell is at genuine 100% capacity (the optimal moment for peak battery life and BMS recalibration).

Formula:
True Full = Status FULL || (chip_soc ≥ 100 && |I_now| ≤ 80mA)

Why is 25°C normalized capacity critical for precision?

• Lithium Thermal Sensitivity:
Usable chemical capacity in lithium-ion and silicon-carbon cells varies directly with ambient temperature. At low temperatures (e.g. 15°C) electrolyte ion mobility drops, reducing measurable capacity; at 30°C–35°C available capacity increases.

• IEC 61960 International Standard:
To evaluate real battery health over time without seasonal weather distortions (summer vs winter), capacity is normalized to the reference temperature of 25°C using the standard thermal coefficient (α ≈ 0.6%/°C):
C_25°C = C_fcc / [1 + 0.006 × (T_batt - 25°C)]

This value represents pure molecular cell degradation, free from ambient temperature bias.

The Oppo charging management chip (BMS) continuously monitors physical hardware safety registers in real-time:

• Short-Circuit Protection (short_c_hw_status):
Verifies power path integrity between charger, switching circuit, and cell. Detects micro-shorts or insulation anomalies.

• Hardware Thermal Shutdown (OTP - short_ic_otp_status):
Over-Temperature Protection. Hardware-level power cutoff if charging module silicon exceeds critical thermal limits.

• Sub-board Sensors (subboard_temp_err):
Verifies health and readings of thermal sensors on the bottom USB-C charging board.

An "All circuits OK" status confirms the charging circuitry and battery have never suffered electrical or thermal trauma.
